title: cross-functional-roadmap-sync-prep-apr-2026-asha-personal-notes
content:
Meeting: Cross-functional roadmap alignment (Product + Eng + Applied ML) - prep notes
Owner: Asha Patel (Product) — personal prep + follow-ups
Meeting date: 2026-04-06 10:00-11:00 PT (sync with Miguel/Riley/Priya)
Objective: 
- Surface major roadmap asks for Q2 sprint plan; make sure ML onboarding + serving runtime priorities are aligned so we avoid last-minute perf/backfill work.
- Agree on 2-3 triage decisions we can commit to in this meeting (model onboarding order, infra capacity for dedicated, eval gating criteria).
Attendees (expected): 
- Asha Patel (Product)
- Miguel Torres (Eng - Serving Runtime)
- Riley Chen (Applied ML)
- Priya Nair (Product - Console & Rollouts)
- Samir Gupta (Infra / Dedicated)
- Optional: Liz Warren (SRE) if latency SLAs discussed
Agenda (30-40 min core + 20 min overflow):
1) Quick context (5m) — product goals for Q2 (increase adoption of Dedicated, improve inference cost by 15%)
2) Applied ML onboarding pipeline & timelines (10m) — Riley to summarize model candidates, quantization/ops needs
3) Serving runtime capacity and perf expectations (10m) — Miguel to call out kernel work, latency SLO impacts
4) Console/rollouts dependencies (5m) — Priya on rollout UI + canary policies needed by Eng
5) Decision points / prioritization (10m) — commit to ordering & blockers
6) Action items & owners (5m)
Background/context bullets (to drop into meeting quickly):
- Product ask: 3 model families to onboard for hosted + Dedicated by end of Q2: 1) mid-sized dialog model (8-12B) for chat, 2) dense embedding model replacement, 3) reranker candidate. Must support streaming + function outputs for chat use-cases.
- Applied ML constraints: current model artifacts require kernel support for fused attention and fp16 path; quantized variants need KV cache adaptation. Riley says: two models can be quantized with minimal reg, third likely needs fresh kernel work.
- Eng constraints: Miguel flagged ENG-541 (attention optimization refactor) as high-impact but risky mid-Q2; if delayed, perf for long-context prompts will regress ~20% (affects latency SLO).
- Infra/Dedicated capacity: Samir notes capacity pool for Dedicated is ~85% booked in region-us-west; to guarantee canary bursts we need to either reserve more or implement fallback routing policy (region or model variant).
Open questions to raise in meeting (short):
- Which of the three model families has highest product ROI if delayed? prioritize? (Product view: dialog > embeddings > reranker)
- Can Applied ML provide a quantized baseline (FP8/INT8) that Eng can validate within 2 sprints? Riley to confirm by 2026-04-09.
- If ENG-541 slips, do we accept higher latency for long-context or postpone one model onboarding? Need explicit trade-off tolerance (ok to increase 99th by +30ms?).
- Can console rollout support per-customer traffic shaping by 2026-05-01? (Priya to confirm dependencies: API for per-route quotas + canary gates)
Proposed decisions for meeting (prep to push):
- Decision A: Prioritize dialog model onboarding first, embeddings second, reranker third. (Rationale: product adoption funnel relies on chat demos; embeddings can be backfilled).
- Decision B: If ENG-541 not merged by 2026-04-20, postpone long-context onboarding and ship short-context quantized variant for canary.
- Decision C: Approve dedicated capacity reservation increase (Samir to propose commit size) if expected Q2 usage > 90% by 2026-04-10.
Risks & mitigations (quick bullets):
- Risk: Kernel work spills into user-facing regressions. Mitigation: add perf regression harness for nightly runs (ENG-PR-402 harness + perf dashboard).
- Risk: Applied ML quantization causes quality regressions. Mitigation: tie eval gating to prompt-set A/B (Riley to add evals to APPL-233).
- Risk: Capacity constraints in us-west. Mitigation: automatic fallback routing config + notify account teams of potential capacity windows.
Action items (populate during meeting; pre-seeded below):
- Action 1: Riley to present short writeup comparing quantized vs FP16 perf/quality for the three models, with sample eval metrics (precision@k, latency) — due 2026-04-09. (linked: APPL-233)
- Action 2: Miguel to surface list of kernel changes required for each model, rough estimate in engineer-weeks, and call out which are must-have vs nice-to-have — due 2026-04-13. (linked: ENG-541, runtime PR #402)
- Action 3: Samir to run capacity forecast for Dedicated (region-us-west) and propose reserve commit or routing policy by 2026-04-10. (linked: capacity-runbook / CONF page)
- Action 4: Priya to validate console rollout APIs for per-route canary and estimate UI work — due 2026-04-12.
- Action 5: Asha (me) to update product roadmap doc and reflect decisions + owner commitments after the meeting — due 2026-04-07. (linked: Confluence Roadmap Q2 2026)
- Action 6: Miguel + Riley to scope regression harness and perf-dashboard inputs; quick spike to prove nightly reg check by 2026-04-15.
Notes-to-self / things to remember in meeting (shorthand):
- Keep convo focused on 2-3 commit points, avoid diving into low-level perf blooms unless Miguel asks for short clarifying examples.
- Push for dates not vague "ASAP" — write down explicit sprint numbers or calendar dates.
- If Priya says API work is >2 sprints, ask for minimal temporary workaround (manual canary by feature-flag).
- Watch for "perfect" quantization ask — remind the group we can ship first with FP16 and iterate.
Follow-up template (post-meeting):
- Email summary + decision list + action-item table (owner / due / jira id) to attendees and exec stakeholders (copy Liz/Wes).
- Update Confluence roadmap page + mark which items need executive buy-in for budget (Dedicated commit).
- Kick a short Slack thread in #product-roadmap with a 2-line decision summary and link to notes.
Potential linked tickets to mention during meeting (short list):
- ENG-541 (attention optimization refactor)
- APPL-233 (quantization evaluation for Q2 model family)
- PROD-812 (roadmap entry: Dedicated onboarding priority)
- runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/402 (perf spike + kernel changes)
Prep checklist (what I need before meeting):
- Riley: short quantization summary (email/one-pager) — confirm 2026-04-09
- Miguel: high-level engineering estimate (sprint-weeks) — confirm by 2026-04-13
- Samir: capacity forecast or decision threshold — confirm by 2026-04-10
- Priya: console dependency list or workaround note — confirm by 2026-04-12
- Me: update roadmap slide deck with proposed order + ROI bullets (1 slide) — finish by 2026-04-05
Loose thoughts / brainstorming (scratchpad):
- Could we offer a "short-context" dedicated SKU (cheaper, lower mem) while long-context modeled workloads are blocked? Might reduce infra pressure and unblock customers.
- Explore using quantized embedding-only path as a stopgap for search use-cases if reranker delayed.
- If customer-critical, offer private deployment pilot for one large account (paying for reserve) to smooth capacity spikes. Need legal/finance to sign.
- Think about a "canary pack" approach: small set of customers get early access; requires per-customer routing + billing flags. Ops overhead tradeoff.
Quick summary to read at meeting start:
- We need to pick: (1) model onboarding order (2) contingency plan if ENG-541 slips (3) capacity reserve decision. Come prepared with hard dates.
Next steps after meeting (my immediate follow-ups):
- Send meeting notes + actions within 24h.
- Update Confluence + roadmap slides.
- Schedule deep-dive with Miguel/Riley if kernel work >2 sprints.
-- end of notes --
